Chapter 10: Continuing the Tradition—The Future of Hymns.
Traditions aren’t just old stories—they’re alive. They grow and adapt, changing with every new generation that picks them up. And the hymns of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints? They’re no different. The heart of the messages stays the same, but the way people share and experience that music is always evolving.
Lately, we’ve seen new hymns added to the collection. Isn’t it fascinating how some of these songs speak directly to today’s challenges, offering hope and a bit of guidance in a world that can sometimes feel overwhelming? Others reach across borders, blending in rhythms and languages from around the globe. For so many, these changes are proof that faith is alive—open to new voices, new stories, and fresh ways of showing devotion.
Now, think about how technology has changed everything. With digital hymnbooks, online recordings, and even virtual choirs, people can stay connected no matter where they are. Imagine families singing together over a video call, even if they’re miles apart. Or someone who can’t make it to church, still joining in worship through music at home. Singing together isn’t just for those in the same room anymore—it’s for anyone, anywhere.
But here’s something to remember: the real purpose of hymns hasn’t changed. Whether you’re in a big cathedral or your own living room, the music still invites everyone to worship, to learn, and to feel connected. The melodies and words offer comfort and hope, reminding us that faith is a journey—and none of us has to walk it alone.
Looking ahead, hymn singing will keep evolving. There’ll be new songs, new voices, and new stories. But at its core, this tradition is about reaching for something higher—connecting with the divine, building community, and finding meaning through music.
Most people don’t realize just how much the future of hymns depends on the choices we make right now. Every time you sing a song, you’re helping renew the tradition. Every new hymn written or shared keeps the story going. In this way, the hymns of the Church become more than just music—they’re a living legacy, a gift for future generations, and a reminder that faith is always growing, always reaching upward.
